target_customer: Independent online tutors and online teaching businesses, with parents paying tutors through the platform
problem: Zoom suits adults but does not hold the attention of young children in online classes, and tutors lack a purpose-built virtual classroom.
business_model: SaaS subscription tiers for teachers and teaching businesses (Koala Pro, Koala Business) plus a marketplace for activities and class booking
product_category: Gamified 3D virtual classroom for online tutoring

founders.name: Xavier Lesage Moretti
founders.background_notes: Born and raised in Paris per the YC page. Education not listed.

founders.name: Benjamin Roux
prior_employers: Apple (described as ex-Apple engineer in the YC launch post)
founders.background_notes: No further background on the YC page.

competitors.name: Zoom
competitors.what: General video conferencing used for online kids classes
competitors.traction_then: Default tool for online tutors and classes during and after 2020

technical_complexity.rationale: Real time video, a 3D room with avatars, whiteboard and co-browser in the browser, built on existing web real-time tooling.

defensibility.rationale: Many virtual classroom tools exist; tutor habits, student engagement and marketplace content give mild lock-in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying the wedge; tutor guides in later years still compare Koala Go to Zoom.

market_need_then: Remote teaching and tutoring grew sharply after 2020 and the YC post says kids disengage on Zoom; the product claimed thousands of teachers by the batch.

branding.domain_note: Uses teachwithkoala.com and learnwithkoala.com rather than koala.com; many unrelated companies are named Koala, including a B2B sales startup acquired by Cursor in 2025.

identity.logo: Koala logo; no mascot character described on the site
identity.visual_style: Playful, kid friendly 3D room with customizable avatars
identity.voice_and_tone: Fun and engaging, tagline Goodbye Zoom Boredom

branding.community_and_virality: Tutor community, a Facebook group, YouTube and social accounts, and a weekly live demo webinar per the company site; independent tutor blogs write about switching from Zoom to Koala Go.

brand_strength.rationale: Friendly name and clear Minecraft analogy, but the name is shared with many companies and the only brand coverage found was niche tutor blogs.

pivots.from: Koala Go virtual classroom for online tutors
pivots.to: Added Learn with Koala, bookable live classes for kids
pivots.why: YC launch post announces it as a new product; whether it replaced Koala Go is not stated.

outcome_analysis: Koala is listed Active with a small team and sells a gamified classroom to online tutors. No dated round, revenue figure or exit was found, so its trajectory is not measurable from public sources. It targets a niche of independent tutors and ESL teachers where Zoom is the incumbent, and the post-2022 decline of pandemic-era remote teaching is a plausible headwind that no source confirms.
notes: Funding unverified: VCBacked lists a 2.5M seed in April 2022 with big-name investors, CB Insights lists 500K and may track a different Koala; both are single aggregator snippets, so no round is recorded. Founding year 2020 per YC; one source says the platform started in 2018. Competition search found only 2024 or later comparisons, so only Zoom (named in the YC launch post) is listed. Acquisition and shutdown results for Koala concern an unrelated sales-intent company. Founder education not found.
